openings.claim: Convert record loss into a review-control signal: adverse transform-record removal → unchanged-manifest coverage gap → widen the affected divergence interval and prioritize available boundary evidence. Digest comparison and the evidence ledger remain the carriers.
openings.delta: Change the dependency for a definite stage claim from finding a differing digest to establishing its earliest supported boundary using cited records and explicit coverage. Index identifiers against the manifest, compare corresponding recorded digests, and keep observed mismatch separate from explanation. Equal input plus unequal output can support a stage mismatch only with evidence excluding an earlier divergence; otherwise report an interval. Timestamp disagreement becomes an uncertainty annotation, never proof of reordered execution.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival—a manifest-ordered digest ledger that notes gaps without changing review priorities—the conversion should identify which claims lose support after removal and redirect bounded inspections. Differing observations are final stage/interval reports, cited support and inspection counts; accuracy or narrower intervals are not guaranteed. Both workflows may produce identical intervals when available records cannot discriminate.
openings.probe: Use the disjoint three-pair subsets to compare rival and conversion workflows; allocate six inspections to each variant per pair, logging every manual inspection, so their combined total stays at twelve. Process all six pairs within sixty minutes and use the additional twenty minutes for comparison. Apply the stipulated random removal to two pairs before final outputs freeze; keep manifests unchanged. Freeze reports, references and resource-fitting next checks before opening the two answer sheets. Assess boundary containment, unsupported definite claims and inspection use. Test false signals by checking a flagged gap against identifiers already indexed: an indexing mistake must not trigger a loss claim. Cancellation occurs when available evidence already supports the same interval. Breakdown occurs when the six-inspection comparison allowance leaves necessary boundaries unread; report unresolved rather than infer absence or exceed the cap.
assumptions: The supplied environment can index the bounded records without adding records.
A next check may inspect an existing uninspected boundary only within remaining allowance; exhausted evidence is explicitly unresolved.

assessment: One testable control conversion; this is a synthetic probe, not deployment or measured improvement. Missing records limit support without proving nonexecution.
